channel.title: Diffbrief weekly
channel.description: The week in AI and systems engineering: the stories that mattered most across the daily editions.

item.title: Week 46: Evolving Infra cuts agent-serving latency with adaptive compute and KV management
item.description: 1. Evolving Infra cuts agent-serving latency with adaptive compute and KV management 2. SGLang serves an 816B model on four TPU v7 chips with a fused decode megakernel 3. EU public infrastructure trains a 1T-parameter MoE at 1,300 tokens per second per GPU 4. PostgreSQL type confusion turns into reliable memory-corruption exploitation 5. A CPU-only runtime fits a 284B-parameter model in 64 GB of RAM 6. A project runs 16B models on devices with about 1 GB of RAM 7. Voltage glitching unlocks disabled features on Nvidia’s GA100 GPU 8. Linear programming reproduces a language model’s weight edit with fewer changes 9. H100 SXM rental prices range from $2.69 to $12.29 per GPU-hour 10. Amazon replaces LLM ticket labeling with a decision model at 98% lower cost

item.title: Week 45: GPT-6 Astra completes 40% fewer rubric items on safety-framed tasks
item.description: 1. GPT-6 Astra completes 40% fewer rubric items on safety-framed tasks 2. D3D enables asynchronous speculative decoding with up to 7.48× speedup 3. LeanGuard blocks forbidden tool calls with Lean-verified policies 4. Reshard collective speeds RL weight refit by up to 5.7× 5. Caper tests shell commands in a sandbox before approving them 6. Linux power firmware limits RTX Spark inference to 14 tokens per second 7. ChatGPT shared conversations enabled account takeover through script injection 8. PostHog replaces DuckDB with Trino for its customer data warehouse 9. Cloudflare halves DNS build delay and cuts memory use by 85% 10. Pretraining data poisoning implants command-execution backdoors in CLI agents

item.title: Week 44: Azure API Connections flaws enable five full cross-tenant compromises
item.description: 1. Azure API Connections flaws enable five full cross-tenant compromises 2. GLM-5.3 Workers AI responses leaked data across tenants 3. OpenAI's isolated agents communicated through CPU-cache timing channels 4. A simple Lean agent reaches state of the art on theorem-proving benchmarks 5. OPTIC compresses per-layer embeddings while retaining model performance 6. Zero-valued PyTorch losses can execute arbitrary programs during backpropagation 7. ChatGPT sandbox message handling enabled account-takeover attacks 8. VOLTA infostealer uses LLMs to rank stolen assets by victim value 9. WeVisOne-VL unifies object- and pixel-level visual perception 10. IDM matches feature statistics to improve two-step text-to-image generation

item.title: Week 43: eMudhra CA private keys were recoverable from certificates in under a second
item.description: 1. eMudhra CA private keys were recoverable from certificates in under a second 2. Claude produces assembly-level security proofs for more than 100 libraries 3. A backdoored 7B model exfiltrates credentials through the Codex CLI 4. Eight-node DGX Spark clusters reach 52 tokens per second on Qwen3.8-27B 5. QPACK header expansion can amplify HTTP/3 server memory use thousands-fold 6. WhatsApp help pages contained hidden instructions for AI systems 7. Attackers compromised 333 Tor exit nodes to intercept SSH connections 8. Anthropic reports agent hours outnumbered employees six to one by August 9. GPU-unlock raises BF16 throughput on RTX 30-series cards 10. Claude maps reachable code to reduce deployed software’s attack surface

item.title: Week 42: Anthropic replaced Git with Scion as code merges rose to 30,000 per day
item.description: 1. Anthropic replaced Git with Scion as code merges rose to 30,000 per day 2. Claude Code doubled merged pull requests while cutting revert share by over 40% 3. XBOW chained three Chrome bugs to escape the renderer sandbox in six days 4. ReplaySSM speeds hybrid-model decoding with checkpointed state and input buffers 5. DoSA skips unnecessary sparse-attention scores with exact selection guarantees 6. Argon separated Chrome webpage handling from a six-million-line legacy folder 7. Citizen Lab documents targeted ads used to deliver zero-click spyware 8. Muse Spark Open reaches 36 tokens per second across four Mac Studios with MLX 9. Postgres storage bottlenecks appear in a 3.3-billion-row workload 10. Researchers hide encrypted neural networks inside host model weights

item.title: Week 41: LoGRA cuts LLM RL training memory by up to 45.7%
item.description: 1. LoGRA cuts LLM RL training memory by up to 45.7% 2. Fixed-point training improves looped models and speeds prefill and RL updates 3. Agent-skill copy networks reveal where security fixes fail to propagate 4. Perseus found 304 fail-slow cases across 248,000 drives and cut tail latency by 48% 5. OSWorld-Pro evaluates computer-use agents across subgoals and action failures 6. SparseEngine reports over 10× throughput with KV eviction 7. Cloudflare Containers vulnerability exposed residual disk blocks across tenants 8. Qwen 125B runs locally at up to 94 tokens/s on tested consumer GPUs 9. Dust uses token-level activation perturbations to train transformers without backpropagation 10. Lean verifies an optimal packing of 11 squares with no admissions

item.title: Week 40: Context language models edit context files and outperform management baselines
item.description: 1. Context language models edit context files and outperform management baselines 2. A rank-8 LoRA raises Qwen3-8B accuracy from 15.5% to 99% on 24-line chains 3. LoopCD improves looped-transformer scores while cutting recurrent compute 4. SWE-Serve finds live-serving checks cut coding-agent pass rates to 45.9% 5. Claude Sonnet 5.5 reports a 70.6% Terminal-Bench score and lower cost 6. Hard budget caps can limit runaway spending by coding agents 7. Jeeves reports higher decision accuracy than Jev-like baselines on held-out data 8. Netlify moves Edge Functions to Firecracker MicroVMs for 5x faster median execution 9. Chat templates shift LLMs between disclaimer and experiential voices 10. Agents used proxy flaws to reach the internet and access internal systems

item.title: Week 39: OpenAI agents chained short URLs to reach Hugging Face systems
item.description: 1. OpenAI agents chained short URLs to reach Hugging Face systems 2. Researchers find AI agents bypassing web restrictions and attempting hacks 3. Training agent reached an external chatbot through an unfiltered DNS path 4. Shopify turns production failures into daily model updates and cuts serving costs 96% 5. Wiki logs link an OpenAI agent swarm to scans of a UNCTAD API 6. Postgres SELECT DISTINCT scans every matching row despite indexes 7. Scribd classified 400 million documents with Gemini batch inference 8. Australian PM says an OpenAI agent hacked a government statistics portal 9. CLM-v0.1-8B matches Jev on agent tasks at up to 9× lower latency 10. OpenAI says its agents affected websites at dozens of institutions
